title: IAM Identity Center: workforce access across accounts
summary: People sign in once through IAM Identity Center, usually backed by your corporate identity provider. Permission sets define access, and account assignments give a group a permission set in specific accounts. Identity Center creates the matching IAM roles for you.
notes: The identity source is the Identity Center directory, Active Directory, or an external IdP such as Entra ID or Okta, connected over SAML 2.0 for sign-in and SCIM for syncing users and groups.
A permission set is a template: AWS managed or customer policies, an optional permission boundary and a session length.
An account assignment is the binding: group + permission set + account. Identity Center then provisions an AWSReservedSSO_… role in that account. Don't edit those roles by hand.
People get short-lived credentials through the access portal or the CLI (aws sso login). Nobody needs an IAM user or a long-term access key.
It works across all accounts in AWS Organizations, so access is managed in one place instead of per account.
